item.title: U.S. Warns Peru is ‘Losing Sovereignty’ Over Chinese-Owned Chancay Port
item.description: The Trump administration warned that Peru is losing sovereignty over a Chinese-owned port near its capital city, after a local judge ruled that the port is exempt from some regulatory oversight.

item.title: Two US Navy Ships Collide, No Major Injuries, US Southern Command Says
item.description: A U.S. warship and a Navy supply vessel collided during refueling Wednesday afternoon, the U.S. Southern Command told Reuters in an emailed statement on Thursday.

item.title: Gas-Hungry Europe to Get Rare LNG Shipment Reloaded From China
item.description: A liquefied natural gas shipment reloaded from China — the world’s top buyer of the fuel — is heading to Europe, a rare move that highlights the continent’s push to refill dwindling inventories.

item.title: Container Rates Slide for Fifth Week as Lunar New Year Demand Disappoints
item.description: Global container shipping rates fell for a fifth consecutive week as the usual pre-Lunar New Year cargo surge failed to materialize, prompting carriers to ramp up blank sailings across major trade lanes.

item.title: HMM Remains Profitable in 2025 Despite Global Freight Rate Collapse
item.description: South Korea’s HMM managed to stay in the black through a bruising 2025 for container shipping, posting a 13.4% operating margin even as freight rates collapsed across major trade lanes and several global rivals slipped into losses.

item.title: Fatal German Bight Ship Collision Was ‘Wholly Avoidable,’ MAIB Says
item.description: Five sailors are dead because no one acted in time. A final investigation into the German Bight collision that sank the cargo ship Verity finds basic collision rules were ignored, decisive maneuvers were delayed, and shore-side intervention came too late to stop a preventable tragedy.

item.title: CK Hutchison Escalates Legal Battle Over Panama Ports Ruling
item.description: Hong Kong-based CK Hutchison has escalated a legal fight over its Panama Canal port concessions, triggering treaty arbitration and raising uncertainty over operations at the Balboa and Cristobal terminals as Panama advances plans for a forced transition.

item.title: Mexican Ships Deliver Food and Supplies to Cuba as Island Faces U.S. Fuel Supply Crackdown
item.description: Two Mexican-flagged ships delivered 814 tons of humanitarian aid to Havana Harbor on Thursday, defying U.S. pressure after Washington threatened tariffs on countries supplying oil to Cuba. Mexico halted oil shipments in January but pledged food assistance.

item.title: Maersk’s Record-Setting Dual-Fuel Containership Goes LEGO
item.description: The Danish toy giant LEGO is set to launch a new collector’s set celebrating Maersk’s methanol-powered flagship, Ane Maersk. The Maersk Dual-Fuel Container Vessel (40955) hits shelves on March 1, bringing the world’s first...

item.title: Navy Collision During Replenishment Draws Attention to Complex At-Sea Operations
item.description: The Arleigh Burke-class guided missile destroyer USS Truxtun (DDG-103) and the fast combat support ship USNS Supply (T-AOE-6) collided during a replenishment-at-sea operation in the Caribbean on Tuesday afternoon, according to U.S. Southern Command.
